```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(gt)
library(readr)
library(here)

# The data set: one row per student on the fall census date.
# This one is invented (3,000 made-up students) so it works on any machine.
census <- read_csv(here("data", "fake_fall_census.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## The data

```{r}
#| echo: true
nrow(census)
head(census, 5)
```

## The question

::: {.callout-note title="IPEDS Fall Enrollment, Part A, line 1"}
Full-time, first-time, degree/certificate-seeking undergraduate students,
by race/ethnicity and gender.
:::

**The rule, in words.** Undergraduate level; full-time; first-time;
degree-seeking. One count per race and gender.

## The answer

```{r}
#| label: part-a-line-1
#| echo: true
a1 <- census |>
  filter(level == "Undergraduate",
         attendance == "Full-time",
         first_time == "Y",
         degree_seeking == "Y") |>
  count(race, gender) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = gender, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(Total = Men + Women)

a1 |>
  gt(rowname_col = "race") |>
  tab_header(title = "Part A, line 1")
```

That is the submission for this line: the question, the rule, the code,
and the numbers, in one file. Next year, change the data file and Render.

## The same thing against your warehouse

Not run here, because there is no database in the room. The only change
is where `census` comes from. The filter and the count stay the same.

```{r}
#| label: from-the-warehouse
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
con <- DBI::dbConnect(odbc::odbc(), dsn = "MY_DSN",
                      UID = "my_user", PWD = keyring::key_get("my_service", "my_user"))

census <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT id, level, attendance, gender, race, first_time, degree_seeking, age
    FROM my_schema.fall_census
   WHERE term_code = '202710'
")
```

Or, if you would rather do the counting in SQL and only show it in R:

```{r}
#| label: count-in-sql
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
qry <- "
  SELECT race, gender, COUNT(*) AS n
    FROM my_schema.fall_census
   WHERE term_code = '202710'
     AND level = 'Undergraduate' AND attendance = 'Full-time'
     AND first_time = 'Y' AND degree_seeking = 'Y'
   GROUP BY race, gender
"
a1 <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, qry)
```

## Try one thing

1. Change the filter to `attendance == "Part-time"`. Render. You just
   answered Part A, line 15.
2. Copy the whole "The answer" section, paste it below, and change the
   filter again. Two questions, two sections. Thirty questions is the
   same file, longer.
3. For a check, add a chunk with `stopifnot(sum(a1$Total) > 0)`.
   If it is ever false, the document refuses to render, which is the
   point.

A full survey file built this way, with checks and an upload file, is
`solutions/ipeds_full_template.qmd`.
